 Learn more US stock futures slouched again on Friday after Anthropic's ( ANT ) successful initial public offering wasn't enough to subdue broad uncertainty over artificial intelligence safety and financing. 
 Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average ( YM=F ) dipped below the flatline after the blue-chip index fell below 50,000 and neared a correction. Those on the S&P 500 ( ES=F ) declined by 0.5% after six consecutive days of losses. Contracts for the Nasdaq-100 ( NQ=F ) fell 1%. 
 Market sentiment was subdued on Friday morning as Asian semiconductor stocks fell , suggesting further tech pressure. Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock fell, extending a six-day decline. 
 A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell from a closing price of $97, though they remain above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can keep the momentum going. 
 Other assets slid on Friday as well. Gold futures ( GC=F ) dropped 4%, while the price of digital gold — bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) — dropped below $62,000 to trade at its lowest price since July. 
 On the economic front, meanwhile, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment will be the highlight, as gas prices have come down to below $4 per gallon. 
 LIVE 2 updates 41 mins ago Grace O'Donnell Dollar near 19-month peak as AI jitters sap risk appetite
 Reuters reports: 
 The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, having risen over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI ‌trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data. 
 The ‌dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025, and was on track for a fourth ​straight week of gains. The rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy. Markets are now pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in December and a small chance of a larger move.
